whatItIs.text: A crisp tree fruit that comes in more than 7,500 cultivars, bred separately for eating raw, cooking, and cider.

historyNote.text: Apple trees originated in Central Asia, where the wild ancestor Malus sieversii still grows; European colonists later carried the fruit to the Americas.

howToChoose.text: Pick firm apples free of soft spots or wrinkled skin, and match variety to job: tart, firm ones hold their shape when cooked, sweeter ones are best for eating.

storage.text: Keep in the fridge crisper, away from anything bruised (one bad apple really does spread). The rulebook has the shelf-life details.
storage.note: crisper storage and when-to-bin guidance live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Soft apples are made for sauce, muffins or a quick spiced compote; peelings dry into crisps or steep into tea.

substitutions.note: similar sweetness and holding power when cooked; softer finish
